summary: Registering a GitHub OAuth app is self-serve, with no GitHub review or payment, so users can connect as soon as the app is registered. The main thing that can hold up launch is that organizations with OAuth app access restrictions block members from authorizing your app.

gates.title: Any GitHub account can register an OAuth app
No test or development mode with limits
No GitHub review before users can connect
Organizations with access restrictions block your app
gates.what: When an organization has OAuth app access restrictions on, its members cannot authorize your app for organization resources. New organizations have restrictions enabled by default.
gates.where: Organization Settings > Third-party Access > OAuth app policy.
gates.todo: Tell users in restricted organizations to request approval for your app from their organization owner.

gates.title: No paid plan needed for production use

requirements.text: A GitHub account, or admin access to an organization that will own the app
A homepage URL for the app
A callback URL for your app (up to 10 allowed)

steps.text: Open Settings > Developer settings > OAuth apps and click New OAuth App.
steps.detail: To own the app under an organization, start from that organization's settings instead of your personal ones.

steps.text: Enter the application name, homepage URL and optional description.
steps.why: These are shown to users on the authorization screen.
A redirect_uri that does not match a registered URL causes an error.
steps.detail: Up to 10 callback URLs can be added.

steps.text: Decide whether to check Enable Device Flow.
steps.why: Device flow must be enabled in the app settings before use.

steps.text: Decide whether to keep Expire user access tokens checked.
steps.why: Expiring tokens last eight hours, and refresh tokens expire after six months without use.
steps.detail: The docs conflict on the default. Check the live form.

steps.text: Click Register application, then copy the client ID and generate a client secret.
steps.detail: Keep the client secret out of client-side code.

steps.text: Prepare the text that tells users in restricted organizations how to request owner approval for your app.
steps.why: Members of organizations with restrictions cannot authorize your app for organization resources.

blockers.problem: Users in an organization cannot grant your app access to its resources.
blockers.fix: The organization has OAuth app access restrictions on. The user requests approval, and an organization owner approves it under OAuth app policy.

blockers.problem: Authorization fails with a redirect_uri error.
blockers.fix: Send a redirect_uri that matches a registered callback URL, or omit the parameter to use the default.
GitHub can suspend apps for reported abuse, spam or API misuse. Contact GitHub Support.
GitHub revokes an OAuth token unused for a year. Send the user through authorization again.

couldNotVerify: Whether Expire user access tokens is checked by default on the live registration form; the pages disagree.

claims.statement: An OAuth app can be registered under a personal account or any organization the developer administers.
claims.sourceTitle: Creating an OAuth app - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: You can create and register an OAuth app under your personal account or under any organization you have administrative access to.

claims.statement: No test or development mode with limits is mentioned on the OAuth app creation page.
claims.sourceTitle: Creating an OAuth app - GitHub Docs

claims.statement: No provider review or verification step is mentioned on the OAuth app creation page.
claims.sourceTitle: Creating an OAuth app - GitHub Docs

claims.statement: Organizations with OAuth app access restrictions block members from authorizing OAuth app access to organization resources.
claims.sourceTitle: About OAuth app access restrictions - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: When OAuth app access restrictions are enabled, organization members and outside collaborators cannot authorize OAuth app access to organization resources.

claims.statement: New organizations have restrictions enabled by default.
claims.sourceTitle: About OAuth app access restrictions - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: When you create a new organization, OAuth app access restrictions are enabled by default.

claims.statement: Owners approve requests under the OAuth app policy in organization settings.
claims.sourceTitle: Approving OAuth apps for your organization - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: In the "Third-party Access" section of the sidebar, click OAuth app policy .

claims.statement: No paid plan is mentioned as required for OAuth app API access; the personal rate limit is 5,000 requests per hour.
claims.sourceTitle: Rate limits for the REST API - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: All of these requests count towards your personal rate limit of 5,000 requests per hour.

claims.statement: No recurring re-verification or audit is mentioned in the token expiration page.
claims.sourceTitle: Token expiration and revocation - GitHub Docs

claims.statement: The form takes a homepage URL and callback URLs, up to 10.
claims.sourceTitle: Creating an OAuth app - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: You can enter up to 10 callback URLs.

claims.statement: A mismatched redirect_uri causes an error.
claims.sourceTitle: Troubleshooting authorization request errors - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: To correct this error, either provide a redirect_uri that matches what you registered or leave out this parameter to use the default one registered with your application.

claims.statement: Device flow must be enabled in the app settings before use.
claims.sourceTitle: Authorizing OAuth apps - GitHub Enterprise Cloud Docs
claims.quote: Before you can use the device flow to authorize and identify users, you must first enable it in your app's settings.

claims.statement: Expiring tokens last eight hours, with refresh tokens expiring after six months without use.
claims.sourceTitle: Authorizing OAuth apps - GitHub Enterprise Cloud Docs
claims.quote: The access token expires after eight hours, and the refresh token expires after six months without use.

claims.statement: The client secret must stay out of client-side code.
claims.sourceTitle: Rate limits for the REST API - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: Never include your app's client secret in client-side code or in code that runs on a user device.

claims.statement: Apps can be suspended for abuse, spam or API misuse.
claims.sourceTitle: Troubleshooting authorization request errors - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: If the OAuth app you set up has been suspended (due to reported abuse, spam, or a mis-use of the API), GitHub will redirect to the registered callback URL using the following parameters to summarize the error:

claims.statement: OAuth tokens unused for a year are revoked.
claims.sourceTitle: Token expiration and revocation - GitHub Docs
claims.quote: GitHub will automatically revoke an OAuth token or personal access token when the token hasn't been used in one year.
